name: Samoan sky
summary: The stars of the “Navigator Islands”: hook, wild duck, kingfisher and sea monster, signs of Polynesian seafaring and of the farming calendar.

001.name: The Cunning Fish
001.description: The Southern Cross. According to the legend, Filo and Mea (Alpha and Beta Centauri) fish for this fish. Not visible from Hungary.

002.name: The Two Men
002.description: Alpha and Beta Centauri: Filo and Mea, the two fishermen hunting the Cunning Fish (Southern Cross). Not visible from Hungary.

003.name: The Three Moons
003.description: The three stars of Orion’s Belt, part of the Carrying Pole. It was the seafarers’ “star path” between Manuʻa and the island of Pukapuka.

004.name: The Wild Duck
004.description: The head of Scorpius: a flying duck which, according to the legend, two star groups (the globular clusters M4 and M80) hunt. The duck’s head, Antares, was also a guide star in navigation.

005.name: The Baited Hook
005.description: The whole hook shape of Scorpius: the magic hook of ʻAloʻalolelā.

006.name: The Pigeon Perch
006.description: The tip of the tail of Scorpius: a figure tied to the noble sport of pigeon catching.

007.name: The Kingfisher
007.description: The constellation Delphinus. According to the legend, the kingfisher ambushes the Grasshopper (the stars of Pegasus).

008.name: The Grasshopper
008.description: The stars of Pegasus: the grasshopper that the Kingfisher (Delphinus) lies in wait for.

009.name: The Carrying Pole
009.description: A long figure from Orion to Monoceros, linked to the legend cycle of Tiʻitiʻiatalaga. The zenith star of the voyage between Samoa and Tonga.

010.name: The Candlenut Torch
010.description: The raised arm and club of Orion: a torch made from the oily nuts of the candlenut (kukui).

011.name: The Tongs
011.description: The horns of Taurus and the Hyades: tongs, linked to the legend of Tiʻitiʻiatalaga (Maui).

012.name: The Sea Monster
012.description: The constellation Cetus (the tail of Cetus is the monster’s head): the monster chases the canoe of the demigod Liʻi, whose face is marked by the Pleiades (Matāliʻi).

013.name: The Ancient War Club
013.description: A long figure from Capella to the stars of the Great Bear.

014.name: The Great Adze
014.description: The “sickle” of Leo: the emblem of Toʻivā, the son of Tapuʻitea (Venus). Venus passes through Leo once or twice a year: this is how the mother visits her son.
